subject: FintechCo  Post-demo performance SLO & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo  Post-demo performance SLO & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time to demo with us on Friday. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on performance/SLOs so we can validate fit and put together a Mutual Action Plan (MAP).

Key requirements you called out during the session:
- Latency: P95 generation latency target <= 250 ms for typical responses (<=256 tokens); P99 target <= 500 ms
- Throughput: sustained 300 QPS for inference, with ability to burst to ~700 QPS during peak windows
- Concurrency: support ~150 simultaneous active streams/requests
- Streaming: yes, streaming responses are required for long-form outputs (progressive tokens and partial results)
- Availability: regional failover (primary us-west, failover us-east), SLA expectations to be discussed in contracting

Attached: SLO checklist (slo-checklist.xlsx) and our initial performance summary from the demo (redwood-performance-report.pdf).

Proposed MAP items / owners / timeline (first pass):
1) Run a 2-hour load test using your sample request set (Dev Patel) — target window next Wed 06/02; deliver: latency/throughput report and bottleneck notes.
2) Canary/dedicated pool config & cost estimate (Rishi Malhotra) — deliver within 5 business days after load test.
3) Short POC: streaming + fallback test (Dev) — 1-week setup, show demo in customer environment.
4) Contract/pricing / SOW discussion (Marissa) — propose term and usage tiers after we validate perf.

Questions for you before we run the load test:
- Can you confirm representative payload sizes (avg and p90 token counts) and a sample query set we should use?
- Any rate-limiters or auth proxies in front of requests we should know about?
- Are there specific security/compliance checkpoints we need run during the POC (e.g., data residency, logging retention)?

If the above looks good I can schedule the load test slot and loop in our infra team.

Best,
Marissa

Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FintechCo  Post-demo performance SLO & next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Below are the clarifications from our side to help make the load test representative.

Workload profile:
- Typical payload: 64 tokens input -> ~120 tokens output (avg)
- Heavy replies (p90): ~400 tokens output (these are the ones streaming matters for)
- Peak concurrent users (observed for last quarter): ~140 active requests, peaking to ~320 during batch jobs

Targets we want to validate:
- P95 (<=256 token responses): <= 250 ms
- P99 (all responses): <= 450 ms
- Sustained throughput: 300 QPS (with ability to scale to 700 QPS for short bursts)
- Concurrent open streaming sessions: 150 (must remain responsive)

Security notes: we have an edge proxy with mutual TLS and a request signing layer; we can provide a test cert and a staging proxy endpoint. Also need to ensure logs can be disabled or scrubbed for POC.

Attached is a small sample of our current call rate by hour (fintechco-current-load.csv) and an exported sample query set.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can your streaming implementation support partial-token delivery and early flush if the model produces a high-confidence answer early?
2) For the canary/dedicated pool — do you have a recommended VM/GPU profile for the above workload or should we run a profiling pass first?

Happy to jump on a quick tech follow-up with Dev next week if helpful.

Best,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering | FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

Alex / Priya —

Appreciate the details — this is exactly what we need. Quick responses inline and an updated MAP with owners/times: 

Answers / commitments: 
- Streaming: Yes — Redwood streaming supports partial-token delivery and can be configured to early-flush when a confidence heuristic fires. We will include the early-flush behavior in the POC and document the tradeoffs.
- Profiling & GPU recommendations: We'll run an initial profiling pass during the 2-hour load test and provide recommended dedicated pool sizing (GPU type, # of replicas) in the follow-up cost estimate.

Updated MAP (owners & target dates):
- 2-hour load test using your sample set (Owner: Dev Patel) — Tue 06/01 10:00-12:00 PT. Deliverable: detailed latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99), throughput graphs, KV/cache hit rates, and notes on streaming throughput.
- Canary dedicated pool & cost estimate (Owner: Rishi Malhotra) — draft by Fri 06/04. Deliverable: cloud profile & monthly cost estimate for reserved capacity + burst plan.
- POC: streaming + fallback scenario (Owner: Dev Patel) — POC build 06/07-06/11; demo 06/14. Deliverable: recording + runbook for integration.
- Contract/pricing / SOW draft (Owner: Marissa Cole) — initial draft by 06/09.

Action items for FintechCo:
1) Share sample queries + confirm token distribution (Alex) — ideally by EOD Mon 05/31 so we can prepare test harness.
2) Provide staging proxy cert or test endpoint if you want the test to run through your proxy (Priya) — before 06/01 test slot.

I've scheduled the tentative load test window in our calendar and invited Dev + infra. If anything needs shifting, let me know and we can move the window.

Thanks — looking forward to running the test.

Marissa
